As these savage and uncivilized cowboys are unwilling to cooperate with the Marketing Development Department, we have no choice but to assume administration of this world on their behalf. We are running out of time. You are permitted to use military force and bring civilization to this world." A terrifying thought rushed into his mind. He frantically ran out. Around him, the employees were still joking and laughing. He held his breath and stifled his rage and tears... His family still needed him. He could not just stop here. Cannon fire rained down from the heavens. By the time he stumbled back to the farm that had now been reduced to ashes, the elderly Graey and Nick, as well as all the friends he'd grown up with, had already lost their lives to the sea of flames. He held on to a faint glimmer of hope that he would be able to find that tiny figure... She had only learned to walk a while ago and would gently slap at the little wooden guitar he had made for her and giggle. But no. There was nothing. The land was scorched black... he didn't even have time to erect a gravestone for the ones he'd lost. "The Interastral Peace Corporation... The Marketing Development Department..." This sight and these names rang through his mind like a nightmare that went on to be etched into his core. Even if he were to die and be born again, he would never forget this. According to the planetary records of Aeragan-Epharshel, the locals who roamed and farmed the land for generations were wiped out by an unknown disaster. The survivors, mostly frail elderly and youth, now only shelter in smaller and smaller reservations. Okhema, the last city, was a cradle of countless myths.
Once, she was like an innocent nymph, sheltered by law, draped in flowing finery, basking in sky's dawning light. She danced across the earth, listened to the ocean's songs, followed reason's teachings, slipped past suitors' trickery, untouched by strife or death. Through ever more beautiful passages she wandered, and people supported her in her worldbearing...
Until time took her joy, her beauty, her life, and more. A skeleton lies quietly in a stone coffin. Yet beneath ribs carved like white jade, her heart hasn't withered.
Wipe away the dust from that beautiful heart, and listen... listen to the heartbeat preserved for you.

They say that even if a man had ten thousand lives, he would not be enough to resist the Sea of Souls's erosion.

Then, courage washes away the immaturity and cold pride tempered timidity —

And that thin figure stumbled onto the shore. The first ray of the morning sun shines down upon the sea's waters, dyeing it like past blood.

A tale circulates among poets:
A scholar unearthed a scroll of parchment from ruins,
upon which an ancient curse was inscribed.
It could kill anyone in this world,
but first, it would collect its price.
An ambitious rebel recited it,
hoping to curse the emperor to death.
The next day, when servants opened his door,
they found the corpse of the one who spoke the curse.
A beggar on the street recited it,
praying to punish the slave master's crimes.
*tinkle* *tinkle*
That villain dropped dead in an instant,
while the price was just three bronze coins in the bowl.
"Could this curse possess the magical power to judge right from wrong?"
The audience debated loudly, then shook their heads and sighed.
If such a curse truly existed,
why would there still be so much injustice on earth?
